reference_prolog:
% Self-contained SWI-Prolog program encoding:
% - Vermont statute 12 V.S.A.  4854 (writ of possession)
% - The question's factual statement
% - A derived yes/no answer

% -----------------------
% Basic context facts
% -----------------------

state(vermont).
focus_year(2021).

authority(sheriff).  % sheriff is the relevant authority mentioned in the statute

% -----------------------
% Statute translation (deterministic predicates)
% -----------------------

% 12 V.S.A.  4854: If plaintiff is entitled to possession, judgment for possession enters.
% "A writ of possession shall issue on the date judgment is entered, unless ... stay."
statute_12_vsa_4854_writ_issues_on_judgment_entry(yes).

% 12 V.S.A.  4854: "The writ shall direct the sheriff ... to serve the writ upon the defendant and,
% not earlier than 14 days after the writ is served, to put the plaintiff into possession."
statute_12_vsa_4854_writ_directs_sheriff_to_put_plaintiff_into_possession(yes).

% Derived legal meaning from  4854: the "writ of possession" is a court-issued directive to an authority
% (the sheriff) to execute possession for the plaintiff (which operationally requires removing the tenant/defendant).
legal_writ_of_possession_is_court_order_to_authority(yes) :-
    statute_12_vsa_4854_writ_issues_on_judgment_entry(yes),
    statute_12_vsa_4854_writ_directs_sheriff_to_put_plaintiff_into_possession(yes),
    authority(sheriff),
    !.
legal_writ_of_possession_is_court_order_to_authority(no) :-
    !.

% Helper: "put the plaintiff into possession" implies the tenant/defendant is removed if still in possession.
% This captures the functional equivalence needed for the question.
legal_put_plaintiff_into_possession_implies_remove_tenant(yes) :-
    statute_12_vsa_4854_writ_directs_sheriff_to_put_plaintiff_into_possession(yes),
    !.
legal_put_plaintiff_into_possession_implies_remove_tenant(no) :-
    !.

% Combined derived meaning: the term "writ of possession" refers to an order from the court to authorities
% to remove a tenant/defendant (so plaintiff can take possession).
legal_term_refers_to_order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant(writ_of_possession, yes) :-
    legal_writ_of_possession_is_court_order_to_authority(yes),
    legal_put_plaintiff_into_possession_implies_remove_tenant(yes),
    !.
legal_term_refers_to_order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant(writ_of_possession, no) :-
    !.

% -----------------------
% Scenario translation (facts + a summarizing predicate)
% -----------------------

% The question asks whether the term 'Writ of possession' is used to refer to:
% "the order from the court to the authorities to remove a tenant".
scenario_term(writ_of_possession).
scenario_claimed_meaning(order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant).

% Succeeds when the factual statement (the question's described meaning) is the scenario we encoded.
scenario_statement :-
    scenario_term(writ_of_possession),
    scenario_claimed_meaning(order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant),
    !.

% -----------------------
% Answer derivation (must not hardcode)
% -----------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    legal_term_refers_to_order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant(writ_of_possession, yes),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    scenario_statement,
    legal_term_refers_to_order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant(writ_of_possession, no),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    % Fallback for unexpected missing scenario facts (kept deterministic).
    !.

% -----------------------
% Main entrypoint (REQUIRED)
% -----------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Is the term 'Writ of possession' used to refer to the order from the court to the authorities to remove a tenant?
